recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. Any future active-resource naming changes should be handled as a new current workflow/resource-specific issue rather than by reviving this retired Order-resource ballot motion.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive with Modification DSTU1 OO ballot comment asking to harmonize inconsistent order/request naming, with a 2015 OO/PC/CDS motion to change referral/procedure/device use/communication request names toward order names.
initial_application: No source commit explicitly mentioning FHIR-5283 was found. The retired Order wording was later removed when Order/OrderResponse were removed for FHIR-10059 and request-resource renaming was applied for FHIR-10295; FHIR-7389 later repeated the same concern and resolved no-change because Order had been retired.
additional_context: Later final decisions supersede the DSTU1 order-name motion: FHIR-10059 removed Order/OrderResponse, FHIR-10295 intentionally used [xxx]Request names for resources that can represent proposals/plans/recommendations as well as orders, and FHIR-11092 kept NutritionOrder as a domain-specific exception. Current fhir.ini activates Request, CommunicationRequest, DeviceRequest, MedicationRequest, NutritionOrder, ServiceRequest, and VisionPrescription, while the old request/order targets are removed or subsumed.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. Reapplying FHIR-5283's 2015 name changes would contradict later workflow decisions, and current source has no remaining retired Order-page sentence or active build-scope artifact needing a FHIR-5283 source change.

related_jiras.note: Direct follow-up quoted FHIR-5283 and was resolved Not Persuasive/No Change because the Order resource had been retired.
Removed Order and OrderResponse, eliminating the original target page and contradiction.
Renamed request resources toward [xxx]Request rather than [xxx]Order for workflow semantics covering more than orders.
Kept NutritionOrder as a domain-specific exception to the [xxx]Request naming direction.
